title: Insurance moves: AILA names president, Markel boosts PFR claims
full_text:
Melbourne barrister Darren Ferrari has been appointed president of the Australian Insurance Law Association (AILA), succeeding Melanie Quixley. Meanwhile, Markel Insurance is strengthening its professional and financial risks claims team.
AILA has appointed Ferrari (pictured, left) as president. He succeeds Quixley, who steps down after three years but stays on the board.
Ferrari is a longtime member with more than 25 years’ legal experience, much of it in insurance law. He said he was stepping in with some trepidation, admitting “Mel’s left big shoes to fill”.
His focus over the next 12 months is governance and positioning the 43-year-old organisation for the future.
“What I want to do in the next 12 months is bed down the things we’ve already put in place through our strategic plan and to make sure it continues progressing steadily,” he said.
Quixley’s achievements include overhauling the membership structure, stronger links between the board and state committees, and a new website and member management system.
Ferrari said membership is at a record high, and programs such as Insurance Fundamentals, CORE CPD and the Emerging Leaders Program have been introduced.
“It’s amazing to have seen membership numbers increase by more than 50%, and importantly, to have seen industry membership numbers increase by more than 50%,” Quixley said.
Markel Insurance has appointed Amy Teagle (pictured, right) as senior claims adjuster in its PFR team, effective immediately. Based in Sydney, she reports to Lisa Mitchell, head of claims – Australia.
She will handle complex professional indemnity, directors and officers (D&O), financial institutions, management liability, employment practices liability, crime and other financial lines claims.
She will also work with brokers, insureds, legal providers and underwriters, and support underwriting strategy and product development.
Teagle joins from DUAL Australia, where she was a senior claims officer managing a national portfolio of complex, high-value PFR claims. Her background includes multi-party professional liability proceedings and regulatory investigations.
“Amy has a fantastic breadth of experience across professional and financial risks and is technically strong, but what stood out to me is how friendly, approachable and pragmatic she is,” Mitchell said.
Markel entered Australia in 2023, and Mitchell joined in December 2023 from AIG. It launched local Commercial Professional Indemnity solutions in 2024 and Financial Institutions cover in May 2025, with dedicated claims handlers onshore.
Financial and professional lines have softened in 2026, as expanded capacity keeps downward pressure on premiums. Clients with regulatory exposure or complex professional liabilities have faced more conservative underwriting.
Claims are a different story. Hall & Wilcox says Australian financial lines claims frequency is down, but severity is up, driven partly by legal costs. DWF says ASIC doubled its investigations in 2025.
In April, the Federal Court’s Southernwood v Brambles judgment became the first Australian shareholder class action to succeed at trial on liability, causation and loss. The Full Federal Court backed market-based causation in Crowley v Worley in May.
Both decisions are on appeal, and the High Court’s Zonia ruling was still pending as of late September. Law firms say the shift could raise exposures for D&O insurers.
For brokers, both appointments offer access points: a law association whose membership extends beyond lawyers and a local claims contact for complex PFR matters.
author: Jonalyn Cueto
heading: General Insurance
